messages:
Sara_CS: Customer reports batch rerank responses where candidate lists look cross-contaminated across queries. They say when they send large ndjson batches (>40 lines) results sometimes show a candidate from query B appearing in query C's ranked list. Trace id reported: tr_zeta77.

Maria_Support: Can you paste their sanitized request and the response? Also which client/SDK and Content-Type?

Sara_CS: Payload (sanitized):
```
{"query":"reset password","candidates":["a1","a2"],"request_id":"r1"}
{"query":"shipping policy","candidates":["b1","b2","b3"],"requestId":"r2"}
{"query":"refund time","candidates":["c1"],"request_id":"r3"}
```
Response snippet they received: 
```
{"results":[{"request_id":"r1","ranked":["a2","a1"],"scores":[0.18,0.02]},{"request_id":"r2","ranked":["b3","b1","b2"],"scores":[0.45,0.15,0.10]},{"request_id":"r3","ranked":["b2"],"scores":[0.77]}]}
```
They noticed r3's ranked candidate b2 actually came from r2's candidates.

Dylan_Eng: Did they use the SDK or roll their own client? Any proxies or connection pooling? NDJSON is line-delimited; missing newline or merged lines could cause parser confusion.

Sara_CS: They used a homegrown batcher (python requests, no SDK). They claim they flush per line. They provided a tcpdump fragment: 
```
...
{"query":"shipping policy","candidates":["b1","b2","b3"],"requestId":"r2"}
{"query":"refund time","candidates":["c1"],"request_id":"r3"}
```
Looks well-formed at first glance.

Kevin_Infra: I pulled our shard logs for tr_zeta77 (shard s12). Saw parser warning at 2026-03-12T14:07:12Z: "candidate_buffer_overflow: expected_total=4 observed_total=5" then debug showing parser merged candidate buffers. Log: 
```
[2026-03-12T14:07:12Z] warn parser: candidate_buffer_overflow trace=tr_zeta77 expected_total=4 observed_total=5
[2026-03-12T14:07:12Z] debug parser: last_token=requestId normalized_missing
[2026-03-12T14:07:12Z] info reranker: emitted scores_count=5
```

Dylan_Eng: Hypothesis: a recent parser tightening removed a fallback that normalized camelCase keys. If a line uses "requestId" instead of "request_id", our earlier lenient code closed the previous object. New stricter flow treats the camelCase token as unrecognized when normalizing keys, so it may append the candidates to the prior object's buffer before the object is finalized. That will produce shifted results.

Maria_Support: Can we verify on the raw capture?

Kevin_Infra: Found the exact offending line in their tcpdump: 
```
{"query":"shipping policy","candidates":["b1","b2","b3"],"requestId":"r2"}
```
So yes: camelCase requestId. I scanned the last 48h and found ~6 traces with candidate_buffer_overflow warnings; 3 used requestId.

Dylan_Eng: Repro steps (local):
1) Build ndjson with middle line using camelCase requestId.
2) POST with Content-Type: application/x-ndjson using curl.
Observed: second and third record candidate arrays merge and shift.
Minimal repro: 
```
printf '%s\n' \
  '{"query":"Q1","candidates":["a1","a2"],"request_id":"r1"}' \
  '{"query":"Q2","candidates":["b1","b2","b3"],"requestId":"r2"}' \
  '{"query":"Q3","candidates":["c1"],"request_id":"r3"}' \
| curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank/batch -H 'Content-Type: application/x-ndjson' --data-binary @-
```

Kevin_Infra: Confirmed in our sandbox; new parser reproduces bug.

Dylan_Eng: Fix plan: patch parser to normalize both snake_case and camelCase forms at tokenization time and ensure we finalize object boundaries before appending next tokens. Also add a strict-mode validation that returns 400 on candidate_count mismatch instead of best-effort merging. I'll prepare a patch and tests.

deploy-bot: Hotfix scheduled: rerank-ndjson-parser-normalize to shards s10..s13 at 2026-03-12T15:45:00Z (ETA ~8m). Change: normalize requestId/request_id + strict candidate_count validation.

Maria_Support: Mitigation for customer until patch lands?

Dylan_Eng: Ask them to switch to one of two immediate workarounds: 1) use the official SDK which normalizes keys; 2) ensure request_id is always snake_case; or 3) send as a single JSON array (application/json) which bypasses ndjson parser. Also offer to re-run their original set once we have the hotfix.

Sara_CS: I'll relay workaround and request permission to re-run. Customer wants ETA and impact on SLA.

Kevin_Infra: Patch ETA ~40 minutes. We'll monitor parser warnings and client-reported traces. We cannot modify previously returned outputs; we can re-process input if customer supplies payloads or grants replay permission.

Maria_Support: Action items: @Dylan_Eng push hotfix + unit tests for both key forms; @Kevin_Infra watch for candidate_buffer_overflow logs post-deploy; @Sara_CS send workaround and ask to re-run + ask for original x-request-ids. Close when customer confirms or re-run completed.

Sara_CS: Noted. Will update customer now and mark as urgent. :eyes: (reacted :thumbsup: by Dylan_Eng, Kevin_Infra)
